newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Clinton route switched in security alert.
newsitem.headline: Clinton route switched in security alert.

text.p: Police on Saturday made a last-minute switch to U.S. President Bill Clinton's proposed route from Manila airport to the hotel he will stay at before Monday's APEC summit.
They made the switch after reports that two men may have placed an object inside a traffic signal control box on the original route.
Clinton arrived safely at his hotel by the alternative route and security officials later reported it had been a false alarm.

A senior U.S. official has said Philippine police fear a leftist hit squad may attempt to mount an attack while Clinton and other leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum are here for Monday's summit.

Police found explosives in the arrival area of Manila's international airport on Wednesday. They originally said the explosives had been planted during a security exercise but a leaked intelligence report later contradicted this.
There was no indication who really planted the explosives.
Police guarding Clinton's route from the airport on Saturday reacted after witnesses reported seeing two suspicious-looking men open the traffic signal control box.
"I would rather be laughed at than put my country in an embarrassing position," the police colonel in charge of investigating the incident told a Reuters Television crew at the scene.

President Fidel Ramos has pledged to ensure the safety of the leaders, cabinet ministers and some 6,000 foreign delegates and journalists covering the fourth annual APEC summit and ministerial conference that preceded it.
